items.title: Error bound for a finite simplex and affine slice
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $\Delta_d=\{p\in\mathbb R^d:p_i\ge0,\sum_i p_i=1\}$, let $M:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^r$ be linear, and let $F=\{q\in\Delta_d:Mq=b\}$ be nonempty. There is a finite $H$ such that
$$\operatorname{dist}_2(p,F)\le H\|Mp-b\|_2\qquad(p\in\Delta_d).$$
proof_obligations: Prove a finite constant exists for every nonempty affine slice of the probability simplex, without invoking a general Hoffman theorem.
Use the projection variational inequality on each realized support face and handle the whole-simplex slice.

references.title: D. Bertsekas, MIT 6.253 Convex Analysis and Optimization, Lecture 6
references.locator: Lecture 6, pp. 32–33; existence and variational characterization of Euclidean projections.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; there are finitely many support patterns, and every nearest point is uniquely determined.

items.title: Berry–Esseen bound for a finite independent array
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent, finite-support real random variables with $\mathbb E X_i=0$ and total variance $\sigma^2=\sum_i\mathbb E X_i^2>0$. If $S=\sum_iX_i$ and $\Phi$ is the standard-normal CDF, then
$$\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}\left|\Pr\{S/\sigma\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|\le1088\,\frac{\sum_i\mathbb E|X_i|^3}{\sigma^3}.$$
proof_obligations: Prove the finite-array quantitative CDF bound by smoothing, the Stein equation, an averaged increment estimate, and induction.
Include arrays with zero-variance summands and make the variance normalization explicit.

references.title: Roman Vershynin, Two Friendly Proofs of the Berry–Esseen Theorem, arXiv:1302.4504v2
references.locator: Part II, §§6–11, PDF pp. 9–17; smoothing, Stein ODE, averaged increments, and induction.

items.axiom_use: The Axiom of Choice is assumed through the repository's standard-normal probability-law interface; no further choice is used in the finite-array argument.

items.title: One-letter Gallager and expurgated exponent functions
items.statement:
Let $W$ be a finite DMC from finite nonempty $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal Y$, with rates and logarithms in nats. For an input law $P$ and $0\le\rho\le1$, define
$$E_0(\rho,P):=-\ln\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y}\left(\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}P(x)W(y\mid x)^{1/(1+\rho)}\right)^{1+\rho}.$$
For $\rho\ge1$, define $B(x,x'):=\sum_y\sqrt{W(y\mid x)W(y\mid x')}$ and
$$E_{0x}(\rho,P):=-\rho\ln\sum_{x,x'}P(x)P(x')B(x,x')^{1/\rho}.$$
For every $a>0$, $0^a=0$; thus zero channel transitions and zero Bhattacharyya coefficients contribute zero to these sums. These are one-letter functions at a fixed $P$; the global maxima and rate-dependent exponent functions are separate definitions.
proof_obligations: Define the two finite-DMC one-letter exponent functions and every zero-power convention.
State the parameter ranges and distinguish the one-letter functions from their global input-law maxima.

items.title: Finite-channel mutual information is concave in the input law
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ be finite nonempty sets and let $V(y\mid x)$ be a row-stochastic channel. For an input probability vector $P$, write $I_P(V)$ for the mutual information under the joint law $P(x)V(y\mid x)$. Then $P\mapsto I_P(V)$ is concave: for input laws $P_0,P_1$ and $\lambda\in[0,1]$,
$$I_{\lambda P_0+(1-\lambda)P_1}(V)\ge\lambda I_{P_0}(V)+(1-\lambda)I_{P_1}(V).$$
proof_obligations: Derive the output-entropy minus conditional-entropy formula from finite mutual information.
Prove entropy concavity including probability vectors with zero coordinates.
Deduce concavity of mutual information from the affine output law and linear conditional entropy.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.5; mutual information as output entropy minus conditional entropy and concavity in the input distribution.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 3, §3.1 and Chapter 19, §19.1; finite mutual-information identities and input concavity for a fixed channel.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; all alphabets and sums are finite.

items.title: Finite Pinsker inequality in Euclidean norm
items.statement:
Let $P=(p_i)$ and $Q=(q_i)$ be probability vectors on a finite nonempty set. With natural logarithms and $D(P\|Q)=+\infty$ when $P\not\ll Q$, one has
$$D(P\|Q)\ge \tfrac12\|P-Q\|_1^2\ge\tfrac12\|P-Q\|_2^2.$$
proof_obligations: Reduce finite KL by log-sum to the binary partition where p exceeds q.
Prove the scalar binary lower bound, including endpoint support cases.

references.locator: Chapter 7, §7.4, Theorem 7.10; full finite Pinsker reduction to the Bernoulli case and its scalar integral proof.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the argument involves finite sums and one-dimensional calculus.

items.title: Gallager and expurgated input-law maxima are attained
items.statement: For a finite DMC $W$, the functions $P\mapsto E_0(\rho,P)$ for each $0\le\rho\le1$ and $P\mapsto E_{0x}(\rho,P)$ for each $\rho\ge1$, defined in [[def-it-one-letter-gallager-exponent-functions]], are finite and continuous on the input probability simplex. Consequently, each attains a finite maximum there. At $\rho=0$, $E_0(0,P)=0$ for every $P$.
proof_obligations: Prove continuity of both one-letter functions on the closed input simplex, including zero coordinates.
Prove the Gallager objective is positive and the expurgated objective is bounded away from zero.
Apply compactness only after the objectives are real-valued and continuous.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, complete author-hosted textbook
references.locator: Chapter 22, §22.4*, printed pp. 431–434; finite-DMC exponent optimizations over the input simplex.

references.title: MIT 6.441 Information Theory, Lecture 11, Spring 2010

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the finite input simplex is compact and all selections in the positivity argument are from finite nonempty sets.

items.title: Conditional information variance and DMC dispersion
items.statement:
Let $P$ be an input probability vector for the finite DMC $W$, and let $P_Y(y)=\sum_xP(x)W(y\mid x)$. On cells with $P(x)W(y\mid x)>0$, define $\imath_P(x;y)=\ln[W(y\mid x)/P_Y(y)]$; the denominator is then positive. Put
$$V(P,W):=\sum_{x:P(x)>0}P(x)\operatorname{Var}_{W(\cdot\mid x)}[\imath_P(x;Y)].$$
Let $C(W)=\max_P I(P,W)$ and $\Pi(W)=\{P:I(P,W)=C(W)\}$, the nonempty set of capacity-achieving input distributions. Define
$$V_{\min}(W):=\min_{P\in\Pi(W)}V(P,W),\qquad V_{\max}(W):=\max_{P\in\Pi(W)}V(P,W).$$
The local attainment lemma [[lem-it-dmc-dispersion-attains-minimum]] proves these extrema exist. Dispersion is measured in nats squared. In the normal-approximation theorem on this page only the fixed range $0<\epsilon<1/2$ and premise $V_{\min}(W)>0$ are used.
proof_obligations: Define the conditional variance for every finite-DMC input law with explicit support conventions.
Define the CAID dispersion minimum and maximum and leave attainment to the justified local lemma.

references.locator: §IV, printed pp. 132–134 / PDF pp. 10–12; dispersion and normal-approximation conventions.

items.title: Gallager, random-coding, expurgated, and sphere-packing functions
items.statement:
Let $W$ be a finite unconstrained DMC from finite nonempty $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal Y$, with rates and logarithms in nats. The one-letter functions $E_0(\rho,P)$ for $0\le\rho\le1$ and $E_{0x}(\rho,P)$ for $\rho\ge1$ are defined in [[def-it-one-letter-gallager-exponent-functions]]. Their maxima over the input simplex are attained and finite by [[lem-it-gallager-input-maxima-attained]]. Define
$$E_0(\rho):=\max_P E_0(\rho,P),\qquad E_r(R):=\sup_{0\le\rho\le1}\{E_0(\rho)-\rho R\}.$$
The expurgated function and sphere-packing expression are
$$E_{\rm ex}(R):=\sup_{\rho\ge1}\left\{\max_P E_{0x}(\rho,P)-\rho R\right\},\qquad E_{\rm sp}(R):=\sup_{\rho\ge0}\{E_0(\rho)-\rho R\}.$$
These functions define lower or upper bounds used on this page; they do not assert that an error-exponent limit exists or that the sphere-packing bound applies without its later strict-feasibility hypothesis.
proof_obligations: Define the global Gallager maximum, random-coding function, expurgated function, and sphere-packing expression in nats.
Cite the one-letter definitions and attainment proof before using maxima over the input simplex.
State that these are bounds or expressions and do not imply an exact reliability formula.

references.locator: Lecture 11, §§4–11, PDF pp. 4–12; finite-DMC random-coding exponent and Gallager function.

references.locator: Chapter 22, §22.4*, printed pp. 431–434; random-coding, expurgated, and sphere-packing bounds.

items.title: Average and maximal error reliability exponents
items.statement:
For a finite DMC $W$, $R>0$, and $n\ge1$, set $M_n=\lceil e^{nR}\rceil$. Let $P_k^*(n,M_n)$ be the minimum error probability among length-$n$ deterministic codes of that size under criterion $k\in\{\mathrm{av},\mathrm{max}\}$, where the two errors are those of [[def-fixed-length-channel-code-errors]]. This minimum exists because the encoder and decoder range over finite sets. Define
$$E_k^-(R):=\liminf_{n\to\infty}-\frac1n\ln P_k^*(n,M_n),\qquad E_k^+(R):=\limsup_{n\to\infty}-\frac1n\ln P_k^*(n,M_n),$$
with $-\ln0=+\infty$. An error-exponent limit $E_k(R)$ is used only when the liminf and limsup agree in the extended reals. These are exponents of error probability; the exponent of success probability is a different quantity. No general exact formula for the finite-DMC reliability function is part of this definition.
proof_obligations: Fix the code-size rounding, average and maximal criteria, and liminf/limsup conventions.
Define the error exponent separately from the success exponent, including zero error.

items.title: The capacity-achieving output law is unique
items.statement: For a finite DMC $W$, every input law attaining $C(W)=\max_P I(P,W)$ induces the same output law $Q^*$. This output law is unique even when the capacity-achieving input law is not.
proof_obligations: Expand finite mutual information as output entropy minus a linear conditional-entropy term.
Rule out two distinct capacity-achieving output laws by strict concavity, including zero coordinates.

references.locator: Chapter 19 §19.1 and Chapter 22 §22.1; finite-DMC capacity optimizers and output laws.

items.title: Globally optimized constant-composition and Gallager functions agree
items.statement:
Let $W$ be a finite DMC and fix $\rho>0$. For each input law $P$, define
$$E_{0,\rm cc}(\rho,P):=\inf_{V:\,V(\cdot\mid x)\ll W(\cdot\mid x)}\left\{\sum_xP(x)D(V(\cdot\mid x)\|W(\cdot\mid x))+\rho I_P(V)\right\},$$
where $I_P(V)$ is the mutual information of $P(x)V(y\mid x)$ and terms with $P(x)=0$ are omitted. At $\rho=0$, set $E_{0,\rm cc}(0,P)=0$. Then
$$\max_P E_{0,\rm cc}(\rho,P)=\max_P E_0(\rho,P),$$
with $E_0$ from [[def-it-gallager-and-expurgated-exponent-functions]]. The equality is after optimizing over $P$; it is not asserted for each fixed $P$.
proof_obligations: Prove the row variational formula with zero transition probabilities and support restrictions.
Prove equality only after global optimization over the input law; explicitly exclude a pointwise-in-P identity.
Handle outputs outside the support generated by a minimizing input law.

items.title: Finite-DMC dependence-testing achievability bound
items.statement:
Let $W^n$ be the block channel of a finite DMC, let $P_{X^n}$ be any input law, and let $M\ge2$. Define the charged information density $\imath(x^n;y^n)=\ln[W^n(y^n\mid x^n)/(P_{X^n}W^n)(y^n)]$ on the support of $P_{X^n}W^n$. There is a deterministic length-$n$ code with $M$ messages and average error at most
$$\mathbb E\exp\left(-\left[\imath(X^n;Y^n)-\ln\frac{M-1}{2}\right]_+\right),$$
where $(X^n,Y^n)\sim P_{X^n}W^n$. For $M=1$, a zero-error code exists. The conclusion is an average-error bound and does not by itself bound every message's error.
proof_obligations: Use the strict-threshold decoder with a fixed tie rule and derive the average false-alarm term.
Convert the threshold expression to the dependence-testing expectation, retaining its exact factor one half.
State that the conclusion controls ensemble-average error only.

references.locator: Theorem 17 and its complete proof, printed pp. 15–16 / PDF pp. 14–15.

items.title: Finite-DMC hypothesis-testing meta-converse
items.statement:
Let a finite-DMC code have $M\ge1$ messages and average error $\epsilon$. For any output probability vector $Q_{Y^n}$, let $P_{MY^n}(m,y^n)=M^{-1}W^n(y^n\mid x_m^n)$ be the true joint law and let $\widetilde Q_{MY^n}(m,y^n)=M^{-1}Q_{Y^n}(y^n)$. With the type-II testing function $\beta_\epsilon$ of [[def-finite-hypothesis-testing-beta]], which constrains rejection under its first argument, one has
$$\beta_\epsilon(P_{MY^n},\widetilde Q_{MY^n})\le\frac1M.$$
proof_obligations: State the null/alternative and acceptance/rejection orientation of beta exactly.
Build the test from the code's decoder and verify both its type-I and type-II errors.
Permit singular auxiliary output laws without taking likelihood ratios.

items.title: A CAID's information-density variance equals its conditional dispersion
items.statement:
For every CAID $P\in\Pi(W)$, let $Q^*=PW$ and let $(X,Y)\sim P(x)W(y\mid x)$. For every $x$ with $P(x)>0$,
$$\mathbb E[\ln(W(Y\mid x)/Q^*(Y))\mid X=x]=C(W),$$
and
$$\operatorname{Var}[\ln(W(Y\mid X)/Q^*(Y))]=V(P,W).$$
proof_obligations: Show each row used by a CAID has divergence exactly C(W), not merely at most C(W).
Apply the finite conditional variance decomposition with the common conditional mean.

items.title: DMC minimum and maximum dispersion are attained
items.statement: For every finite DMC, the set $\Pi(W)$ of capacity-achieving input laws is nonempty and compact, and the function $P\mapsto V(P,W)$ is continuous on $\Pi(W)$. Therefore $V_{\min}(W)$ and $V_{\max}(W)$ in [[def-it-channel-dispersion]] are attained.
proof_obligations: Show the capacity-achieving set is a nonempty closed subset of the finite input simplex.
Use the unique full reachable output law to prove continuity of conditional dispersion on that set.

items.title: Finite-DMC information deficit controls squared distance to the CAID set
items.statement:
Let $W$ be a finite DMC, $C=C(W)$, and $\Pi=\{P:I(P,W)=C\}$. There is $\alpha>0$, depending on $W$, such that every input law $P$ satisfies
$$C-I(P,W)\ge\alpha\,\operatorname{dist}_2(P,\Pi)^2.$$
proof_obligations: Derive the exact KL gap identity and identify the CAID set as a finite affine slice.
Combine a positive slack on inactive input letters, Pinsker, and the proved affine-slice error bound.
Treat the whole-simplex CAID case and an empty inactive-input block.

items.title: Gallager expurgated exponent lower bound
items.statement:
For every finite unconstrained DMC and rate $R>0$, the liminf average- and maximal-error exponents satisfy
$$E^-_{\rm av}(R)\ge E_{\rm ex}(R),\qquad E^-_{\rm max}(R)\ge E_{\rm ex}(R),$$
where $E_{\rm ex}$ is defined in [[def-it-gallager-and-expurgated-exponent-functions]]. This is a lower bound; it is not asserted to equal the general reliability function.
proof_obligations: Derive the pairwise Bhattacharyya bound on ML error and tensorize it across a DMC block.
Apply subadditivity for the power 1/rho and expurgate messages with large pairwise sums.
State the resulting guarantee as a lower bound, not an exact low-rate formula.

items.title: Gallager random-coding exponent lower bound
items.statement:
For every finite DMC without an input-cost constraint or feedback and every $R>0$,
$$E^-_{\rm av}(R)\ge E_r(R),\qquad E^-_{\rm max}(R)\ge E_r(R),$$
where $E_r$ is the random-coding function in [[def-it-gallager-and-expurgated-exponent-functions]]. If $0<R<C(W)$, then $E_r(R)>0$. This is an achievability lower bound, not an exact general reliability formula.
proof_obligations: Derive the Gallager moment bound from the ML error event, Jensen, and the DMC product law.
Convert the bound to the liminf average-error exponent and then expurgate for maximal error.
Establish positivity below capacity by differentiating the finite E0 sum at rho zero.

items.title: Sphere-packing converse above the finite-divergence threshold
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $W$ be a finite unconstrained DMC. For $P$ on $\mathcal X$, let $V$ range over row-stochastic channels satisfying $\operatorname{supp}V(\cdot\mid x)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}W(\cdot\mid x)$, and define
$$D_P(V)=\sum_xP(x)D(V(\cdot\mid x)\|W(\cdot\mid x)),\quad I_P(V)=I(X;Y)\text{ under }P(x)V(y\mid x),$$
$$J(P)=\min_V I_P(V),\qquad R_\infty(W)=\max_PJ(P).$$
For every $R>R_\infty(W)$, the limsup average- and maximal-error exponents satisfy
$$E^+_{\rm av}(R)\le E_{\rm sp}(R),\qquad E^+_{\rm max}(R)\le E_{\rm sp}(R),$$
where $E_{\rm sp}$ is defined in [[def-it-gallager-and-expurgated-exponent-functions]]. The theorem makes no endpoint assertion at $R=R_\infty(W)$.
proof_obligations: Define the finite-divergence auxiliary-channel set and the threshold R_infinity; establish compactness and strict feasibility for R>R_infinity.
Prove the constant-composition converse by Fano, a uniform Chebyshev bound, and an explicit change-of-measure inequality.
Pass from arbitrary codes to a type subcode and track the polynomial rate/error loss.
Derive the convex-duality identity only under strict feasibility and keep the AC/CC separation branch explicit.
Use the global constant-composition/Gallager identity, not a pointwise-in-input identity.

references.locator: Chapter 22, §22.4*, printed pp. 433–434; sphere-packing converse and strict-feasibility variational route.

items.axiom_use: This theorem assumes the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice exactly through the published weak-separation supplier; all finite-DMC and type-class steps are choice-free.

items.title: Nondegenerate normal approximation for finite unconstrained DMCs
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $W$ be a fixed finite DMC with no feedback or input-cost constraint, let $0<\epsilon<1/2$ be fixed, and suppose $V_{\min}(W)>0$. For $k\in\{\mathrm{av},\mathrm{max}\}$, let $M_k^*(n,\epsilon)$ be the largest number of messages in a deterministic length-$n$ code with uniform messages and error criterion $k$ at most $\epsilon$. Then
$$\ln M_k^*(n,\epsilon)=nC(W)+\sqrt{nV_{\min}(W)}\,\Phi^{-1}(\epsilon)+O(\ln n),\qquad k\in\{\mathrm{av},\mathrm{max}\},$$
where all logarithms are natural, $\Phi$ is the standard-normal CDF, and the constants may depend on $W,\epsilon$. This theorem makes no claim for cost constraints, $\epsilon\ge1/2$, zero dispersion, or a third-order coefficient.
proof_obligations: State deterministic encoders, uniform messages, natural logarithms, fixed 0<epsilon<1/2, and V_min>0.
Establish uniform local variance/third-moment bounds near the CAID set and a global variance bound.
Prove the constant-composition testing converse with its decoder-region split, then use uniform Berry–Esseen and quantile inversion for near types.
Use the quadratic capacity gap to optimize over nearby types and Chebyshev plus a compactness gap for far types.
Expurgate an arbitrary average-error code to error epsilon+n^{-1/2}, select a type, and track both logarithmic losses.
Prove DT achievability at the minimum-dispersion CAID, then expurgate to maximal error without claiming third-order precision.

items.title: The error exponent is zero above finite-DMC capacity
items.statement:
For every finite unconstrained DMC and every $R>C(W)$,
$$E^-_{\rm av}(R)=E^+_{\rm av}(R)=E^-_{\rm max}(R)=E^+_{\rm max}(R)=0.$$
These are error-probability exponents; no success-probability exponent is asserted.
proof_obligations: Apply the actual average-error strong converse to optimal finite-block codes.
Convert error probability tending to one into both liminf and limsup error exponents equal to zero.
Keep this error exponent separate from a success-probability exponent.

items.title: Small expected average code error need not control maximal error
items.statement: For every integer $M\ge2$, there is a singleton random-code ensemble on a finite noiseless DMC whose expected average error is $1/M$ while the code's maximal error is $1$. Thus a small expected average error alone does not make every message's error small.
proof_obligations: Give a finite DMC code with one message of error one and all other messages correct.
Compute both average and maximal error and realize the code as a singleton random ensemble.

items.title: Exact evaluation of a one-use BSC dependence-testing bound
items.statement: For a one-use BSC with crossover $p=0.1$, uniform input, and $M=2$, the dependence-testing upper bound on achievable average error is exactly $0.35$.
proof_obligations: Compute the information density on both positive-probability BSC events.
Evaluate the positive-part threshold expression exactly, including the tie convention.

items.title: Exact beta value for a one-use BSC meta-converse test
items.statement: For the one-use BSC$(p)$ with $0<p<1/2$, the identity encoder/decoder with two equiprobable messages has average error $p$. With its true joint law $P_{MY}$ and the uniform-message/uniform-output auxiliary law $\widetilde Q_{MY}$, the oriented testing value is exactly $\beta_p(P_{MY},\widetilde Q_{MY})=1/2=1/M$.
proof_obligations: Enumerate true and auxiliary probabilities on all four message-output pairs.
Verify the beta orientation and prove the finite linear program's optimum, including randomized tests.
